decision_lens: Platforms are justified by the products they enable. A platform that generalises ahead of its first validated consumer is building on hypotheses that may not survive contact with the product. The correct sequencing question is not 'platform or product first' but 'what is the minimum platform that enables the first product to validate the platform's core assumptions'.
distance_rationale: Pharma platform development teams face the identical sequencing dilemma: a shared platform (Palettice / the personality engine) supports multiple products (shadow-work, elf-revel, Culture game) at different pipeline stages, with constant pressure to generalise the platform ahead of the next product's needs — they have hard-won heuristics about when platform-first investment is justified and when it delays the validation experiments that would confirm or refute the platform's assumptions.
expected_isomorphisms: The pharma 'platform generalisation must be driven by validated usage, not anticipated usage' principle maps directly onto the brainstorm's expansion items 4-6: they are designed for an unvalidated consumer (the Culture game that may never be built). The pharma 'Phase 1/2/3 go/no-go criteria' pattern maps onto the missing exit criteria for the Palettice expansion phases — the brainstorm identifies six items in dependency order but provides no observable outcome that would indicate each phase succeeded or should be cancelled.
focus: Pharmaceutical platform development patterns for managing a shared platform that supports multiple drug candidates — applied to the migration-vs-demo priority tradeoff, the risk of platform generalisation outrunning validated usage, and the sequencing of pipeline expansion vs. delivery commitments
name: fd-pharma-platform-pipeline-consolidation
persona: Apply the perspective of a pharma platform development lead who has managed a shared chemistry platform across multiple drug candidates in parallel pipelines — they care about whether platform generalisation is driven by validated usage or by anticipated usage, measure platform investment against the risk of the platform never producing a shipped product, and flag whenever a 'platform first' decision delays the first proof-of-concept that would validate the platform's assumptions.
review_areas: Migration-as-platform vs. demo-as-product: the brainstorm's central priority decision is 'migration takes priority over the demo'; a pharma platform reviewer asks: is this the right sequencing given that the platform's core assumptions (31-facet model generalises, event-sourcing works for personality, derivations are the right abstraction) have not been validated by a shipped product?; shadow-work's demo IS the validation experiment for the platform — delaying it delays validation

Platform generalisation ahead of validated usage: the six Palettice expansion items are driven by shadow-work migration (items 1-3) and Culture-game horizon (items 4-6); a pharma reviewer flags that items 4-6 (aggregation Souls, Mind-scale time, LLM-curated naming) are designed for a consumer that does not exist yet; platform investment in anticipated-but-unvalidated consumer needs has a high failure rate — the risk is that the Culture game never ships and items 4-6 represent stranded investment

The 'convergence is the asset' argument: the brainstorm argues that 'three independent game projects landing on the same personality engine shape is a strong signal'; a pharma platform reviewer applies the independent-confirmation test — are the three projects genuinely independent, or do they share a designer whose implicit assumptions drove all three toward the same shape?; the convergence signal is much weaker if the three projects are not independent

Pipeline sequencing and exit criteria: the brainstorm proposes a migration sequence (items 1-3 first, items 4-6 later) but does not define exit criteria for each phase — what observable outcome would indicate that the migration succeeded and items 4-6 should begin?; pharma pipelines require explicit go/no-go criteria at each phase transition

Second-system effect risk: the brainstorm explicitly names the second-system risk ('building the abstractions you imagine you need rather than the ones you've already learned you need') and proposes shadow-work-as-reference as the mitigation; a pharma reviewer asks: is this mitigation sufficient, or does it just relocate the second-system risk to the cultural-game expansion items (4-6), which ARE imagined needs for an unvalidated consumer?

Demo retirement risk and project morale: Open Question 5 raises 'demo retired' as a sub-option compatible with migration priority; a pharma reviewer flags this as a significant morale and validation risk — if the Prometheus Crisis demo is never shipped, the team never gets the external signal (player reaction, blowback emergence, personality-system feel) that validates the engine assumptions; platform investment without a shipped product can sustain for one cycle but not indefinitely

severity_examples.condition: If migration is prioritised over demo and the demo is substantially delayed (months), the engine's core assumptions (31-facet model produces interesting emergent personality, blowback cascade is legible to players, derivation-based archetype computation has acceptable latency) remain unvalidated during the migration; if any of these assumptions fail when the demo eventually ships, the migration may have built on a wrong foundation
severity_examples.scenario: Demo deferral delays the only validation experiment

severity_examples.condition: The brainstorm explicitly states 'the game itself may never be built'; aggregation Souls, Mind-scale time, and LLM-curated naming (items 4-6) are justified entirely by the Culture-game horizon; if the Culture game is not built, these items represent platform investment that no consumer will use; the brainstorm does not define a trigger criterion for when items 4-6 should be deprioritised or cancelled
severity_examples.scenario: Expansion items 4-6 are stranded investment if Culture game is never built

severity_examples.condition: If the convergence between shadow-work and Palettice is driven by shared designer assumptions rather than independent development (the same designer made both systems), the 'three projects converging' argument for platform investment is overstated; the migration may still be the right decision, but the convergence evidence should not be presented as independent validation
severity_examples.scenario: Convergence signal is weaker than claimed

source_domain: Pharmaceutical drug platform development — shared platform supporting multiple drug candidates, pipeline consolidation
